subject: URGENT: Route amplification + proxy throttle causing Checkout latency (ShopFront)
messages:
From: ShopFront Alerts <alerts@shopfront.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: URGENT: Checkout 95p latency spike + 503s impacting checkout flow

Hi Jonas,

We started seeing a sudden spike in checkout latency and 5xx errors around 07:30 PT this morning. The attached histogram shows 95th/99th percentile token latency for Redwood generation calls to our checkout service — the error rate jumped from ~0.4% to ~8% and checkout throughput dropped by ~35%. This is customer-impacting.

What we've observed: 
- Multiple 503/504s coming back from the Redwood endpoint (region-us-west).
- Long tail latency (95p ~1.6s -> 3.8s) on generation calls used in payment validation.
- Errors correlate with increased DNS lookup time for model-serving endpoints.

We tried failing over to the secondary region and saw improved success rates, but this is not sustainable. We need an urgent triage and an executive update — our customers are already contacting support.

Attachments: shopfront-trace-20261120-histogram.png, sample-pcap-20nov.txt

Please advise next steps.

— Alicia Chen
Senior SRE, ShopFront
alicia.chen@shopfront.io
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudOps Partner <cloudops@infra-partner.net>
Date: 2026-11-20T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: URGENT: Checkout 95p latency spike + 503s impacting checkout flow

Team — forwarding ShopFront alert. High priority customer escalation (ShopFront, DF-8742).

Initial notes:
- Customer reports jump in latency + 5xx starting ~07:30 PT.
- They saw improvement when failing over regions which points to a networking/peering path issue rather than model degradation.
- CloudOps partner is CC'd — partner owned peering/config changes happened early this morning (per onboarding notes).

Ask: can SRE validate whether we are seeing:
  1) BGP/peering instability to ShopFront prefixes
  2) DNS resolution timeouts or resolver fallbacks to slower resolvers
  3) Any edge proxy/ACL that could be rate-limiting bursts (we've had throttle signatures before)

I'm standing up a quick bridge for 09:00 PT. Monica — can you lead triage? Marissa/Markus — please gather customer-facing metrics and prepare a short exec summary for Vivek.

Jonas
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudOps Partner <cloudops@infra-partner.net>
Date: 2026-11-20T08:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT: Checkout 95p latency spike + 503s impacting checkout flow

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 08:22, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — forwarding ShopFront alert. High priority customer escalation (ShopFront, DF-8742).

Quick triage update (pre-bridge):
- Observed repeated DNS resolution delays to ShopFront's edge resolver (avg resolution jumped from 25ms -> 420ms) in our region-us-west serving pool.
- Active traces show asymmetric forwarding: packets to ShopFront egress are being routed through an unexpected transit (additional 3 AS hops) and intermittently hit a proxy/inspection appliance that adds ~300–600ms on tail latency.
- Error signatures: downstream 502/504s are originating at our edge-proxy when backlog reaches a certain concurrency threshold — looks like a soft throttle configured at the proxy level.

Attached: aggregated qlog traces and a short pcap extract (sample-pcap-20nov.txt).

Immediate mitigations we can enact (short-term):
1) Temporarily route ShopFront traffic via alternate peering (we have a standby path to partner region) — requires partner approval/roll back window.
2) Bump proxy concurrency ceiling for the affected tenant for 60 minutes.
3) Enable aggressive local DNS caching for ShopFront prefixes to avoid resolver fallbacks.

I'll take the bridge at 09:00 PT and attempt the route change with the partner. Will report back with timestamps and impact metrics.

— Monica
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: CloudOps Partner <cloudops@infra-partner.net>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Checkout 95p latency spike + 503s impacting checkout flow

Monica / Jonas — we investigated and found that a maintenance change (CHG-11207) deployed at 07:45 PT introduced a BGP path preference adjustment for the ShopFront prefix block. That change caused transient route flapping and the traffic to hairpin through a legacy inspection appliance we still run in the path. We are rolling back CHG-11207 now.

Planned immediate actions: 
- Rollback CHG-11207 (started 09:02 PT).
- Temporarily advertise an alternate route to avoid the inspection appliance (will announce at 09:08 PT).
- Validate route stability and remove the legacy appliance from the path by 10:00 PT.

Change record: https://console.infra-partner.net/changes/CHG-11207 (attached pdf).

We expect to see tail latency drop within 20–30 minutes after the rollback and alternate announcement. We will keep the bridge live until confirmed.

— CloudOps Network Ops
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alicia Chen <alicia.chen@shopfront.io>
Date: 2026-11-20T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Exec summary & recommended customer remediation (ShopFront impact) — approval requested

Vivek / Markus — quick exec summary and ask: 

Impact summary (ShopFront, DF-8742):
- Time window: ~07:30–09:40 PT (approx).
- Impact: sustained 95p latency increase from ~1.6s to ~3.6s, 5xx rate peaked at ~8%, checkout throughput down ~35% during peak.
- Root cause (prelim): partner change CHG-11207 caused BGP path preference change; traffic hit a legacy inspection appliance and our edge proxy hit a soft throttle under increased concurrency.

Customer-facing remediation proposed: 
1) Provide ShopFront one week of equivalent hosted capacity credits (to offset measured impact) — estimated credit = one week of committed usage at current unit price.
2) Offer a one-time service credit of 20% applied to last invoice as goodwill.
3) Joint post-mortem within 72 hours with partner invited.

Technical mitigations we will implement immediately: 
- Permanent removal of legacy inspection appliance from ShopFront path with partner (change coordination).
- Harden proxy concurrency limits and add per-tenant safe overrides.
- Improve DNS caching policy for customers with sensitive checkout flows.

Approve the remediation ask so I can communicate to Alicia and coordinate billing.

Jonas
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
